questions.question: What percentage of a presentation should the introduction take?
questions.explanation: The introduction should be about 10-15% of total time, enough to grab attention and preview the content without taking too long.

questions.question: What is "signposting" in presentations?
options: Using transition phrases to guide the audience through your talk
Holding up signs during your presentation
questions.explanation: Signposting uses phrases like "Moving on to..." or "My next point is..." to help the audience follow the structure of your presentation.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good strategy for managing presentation nerves?
options: Reading your entire speech word-for-word from a script
Focusing on your message rather than yourself
questions.explanation: Reading from a script makes presentations less engaging. Practice allows you to speak naturally while knowing your content.

questions.question: What makes a good opening for a presentation?
options: A surprising statistic, question, or story
Reading the title of your presentation
questions.explanation: Strong openings capture attention immediately. A hook engages the audience and makes them want to listen.

questions.question: Why is eye contact important during presentations?
options: It creates connection and shows confidence
It helps you read your notes
questions.explanation: Eye contact engages the audience, conveys confidence, and helps you gauge their reactions.
